sketches.title: Mum Was Right
sketches.premise: Mum texts you a dull, true news fact. Turn it into a wild reply that still leaves her fact standing. The Host awards points for the biggest leap from sensible news to glorious family chaos.
sketches.criterion: The reply must keep the card’s news fact true, even if the reply adds motives, gossip, threats or innuendo.
sketches.move_shape: Write one text reply under 90 characters; example: Card: “The town opened a new footbridge.” Move: “Lovely—now the ducks have somewhere to meet their secret lovers.”
sketches.first_card: The library has added six new chairs.

sketches.title: Mum Forwards This
sketches.premise: Mum sends a true news fact and asks you to make it sound like a message she would forward to the whole family. You score for turning plain reporting into maximum chain-message panic without breaking the fact.
sketches.criterion: The message must retain the card’s exact real-world outcome, while its warning, advice and family drama may be invented.
sketches.move_shape: Write a forwarded-style text under 90 characters; example: Card: “A bakery opened on High Street.” Move: “PLEASE SHARE: the High Street bakery is open—bring cash and emotional support.”
sketches.first_card: A bus company has changed one route.

sketches.title: Dear Mum, Regarding
sketches.premise: Mum texts a small news fact; you answer as if you are a very serious official replying to her. Make the reply oddly formal, personal or filthy-minded, but do not lose the fact in the paperwork.
sketches.criterion: The answer must still state or clearly preserve what the news fact says happened, without adding a false change to it.
sketches.move_shape: Write an official-looking reply under 90 characters; example: Card: “The park got two new benches.” Move: “Noted. Seating has increased; your campaign for nap-based government continues.”
sketches.first_card: The council repaired a broken streetlamp.

sketches.title: Mum Sends a Voice Note
sketches.premise: Mum texts a true news fact, and you turn it into the transcript of a voice note she would send while doing something else. Points reward the strangest believable voice-note world built around the fact.
sketches.criterion: The transcript must leave the card’s event true and recognisable; all side comments, feelings and family accusations are yours.
sketches.move_shape: Write a voice-note transcript under 90 characters; example: Card: “A museum bought a painting.” Move: “Right, the museum bought a painting—anyway, your uncle is banned from auctions.”
sketches.first_card: The zoo welcomed a new tortoise.

sketches.title: Mum Reads the Comments
sketches.premise: Mum sends a dull news fact and you write the comment she would post beneath it. Your comment may be sweet, rude, suspicious or wildly overconfident, but the news must survive the roast.
sketches.criterion: The comment must keep the reported fact true while adding a clear opinion, personal story or jab.
sketches.move_shape: Write one comment under 90 characters; example: Card: “The cinema added a late show.” Move: “Good. Your dad finally has somewhere to nap after dinner.”
sketches.first_card: The swimming pool is closing for one week.

sketches.title: Mum Checks the Receipts
sketches.premise: Mum texts a true news fact and demands a tiny reply proving you understood it. Hide the fact inside a strange receipt, list or bill, then spend the rest on comic nonsense.
sketches.criterion: The entry must contain a checkable version of the card’s fact; invented prices, items, names and reasons are allowed.
sketches.move_shape: Write a receipt or list under 90 characters; example: Card: “The station got a new clock.” Move: “STATION CLOCK £1; punctuality £0; Dad’s excuses, priceless.”
